title: Finitely presented affine replacement with an overlap isomorphism
statement: Let X be a quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], W a quasi-compact open [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], V an affine open, and H a quasi-coherent module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, pqf-def-coherent]. Suppose H restricted to W is finitely presented [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation]. There exists a finitely presented module E on V and a map j from E to H restricted to V whose restriction to W intersect V is an isomorphism. No extension away from V and no glued module is asserted.

proof.text: The overlap K = W intersect V is compact by quasi-separatedness. Restrict finite presentation from W to K using overMap and overFunctorMap; fp_overMap proves the localized-site preservation through continuous left-adjoint pushforward.

Apply exists_finiteType_affine_generators directly to H on K. It gives a map phi from a finite free module on V to H restricted to V, epimorphic after restriction to K. The restriction of its target is finitely presented by the canonical overFunctorMap isomorphism. No finite-type capture of the target or global epimorphism on V is required.

The kernel of phi is quasi-coherent, by transport across overEquiv and isQuasicoherent_kernel. Localized restriction preserves kernels: transport overMap along overMapCompOverEquiv to the open-subscheme restriction functor and use its source-library limit preservation. On K the target H restricted to V is finitely presented and the source is finite free; transport to K.toScheme and apply finitePresentation_kernel_surjection_finiteType. Transfer finite type back to the localized site.

Extend the quasi-coherent kernel from V to an ambient quasi-coherent L using 01PE(3), applied to its zero map into H on V. The returned isomorphism identifies L on V with the kernel; overFunctorMap identifies its restriction on K. Apply affine capture to L on K, producing a finite-type Q on V and a map kappa into the kernel that is an isomorphism on K. No arbitrary existence witness is used as the body of a definition.

Set a = kappa followed by the kernel inclusion and E = cokernel a. The free source is finitely presented using its zero-relations presentation. Transfer a to V.toScheme and apply the finite-type-source cokernel theorem, then transfer finite presentation back through overEquiv. The equation a followed by phi = 0 defines the descent map j from E to H restricted to V.

On K the restricted phi is epi and the preserved kernel fork is limiting, so Abelian.epiIsCokernelOfKernel makes phi the cokernel of the restricted kernel inclusion. Since restricted kappa is an isomorphism, isCokernelEpiComp makes it a cokernel of restricted a as well. Restriction preserves the cokernel defining E. Uniqueness of these two cokernels identifies restricted j with the canonical isomorphism. This j is the required map into H restricted to V.

proof_origin.note: Lean combination of finite generators epimorphic on the overlap, kernel finiteness, quasi-coherent extension, affine capture of the kernel relations, and cokernel uniqueness; follows the affine step of Stacks 01PI. No global finite-type approximation of H is needed.

lean.statement: theorem exists_finitePresentation_affine_replacement (X : Scheme.{u}) [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] (W : X.Opens) (hW : IsCompact (W : Set X)) (V : X.affineOpens) (H : SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) [H.IsQuasicoherent] [(H.over W).IsFinitePresentation] : ∃ E : SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over V.1), E.IsFinitePresentation ∧ ∃ (j : E ⟶ H.over V.1), IsIso ((SheafOfModules.overMap (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) (homOfLE (show W ⊓ V.1 ≤ V.1 from inf_le_right))).map j)
